_what: PERFORMANCE LAW. 8K fidelity dies silently, one asset at a time, without a verifier. Same pattern as the city verifier: the recipe DECLARES, the flythrough MEASURES, the suite ENFORCES.
_order_is_deliberate: MEASURED FIRST, THEN DECLARED. Every budget below started as null and was filled from a baseline capture of the current world. A budget invented before a measurement is a bar chosen to pass the number it first saw -- non-negotiable 2 -- and this project already has one of those on record (max_orphan_building_fraction, set at 0.05 against a measured 3.6%).

target._resolution: the operator's display is 2560x1600 at 150% scaling. 1440p is the honest target for this machine.
target._fallback: stated so a budget breach has a defined retreat rather than an argument
target._frame_budget: RULED 2026-09-10: 16.6 ms, enforced on FrameTime p90 in the STANDALONE class (where FrameTime is a real cost signal, not the editor clamp).

_MEASUREMENT_CLASS_AND_IT_BINDS_EVERY_NU: STANDALONE -game PROCESS, RULED 2026-09-10. The prior class (editor viewport) is REJECTED for budgets: UEditorEngine::GetMaxTickRate clamps the editor to the rate it is already running at (EditorEngine.cpp:2523-2566), FrameTime pins near 16.67 ms, and E3 measured the editor's GameThreadTime tracking that clamp (13.9-14.15 ms at all four zones) while the standalone game thread reads ~3.9 ms -- the editor game-thread figure measured the HARNESS, not the content. check_perf REFUSES an artefact that does not declare the standalone class. The editor viewport remains a fine instrument for RELATIVE work (same-session A/B); it may not source a budget.

spline._what: A FIXED route, so numbers are comparable across sessions. Stations are DERIVED, not chosen by eye -- regenerating them gives the same route.
spline._derivation: plaza from city/alpine_basin_town_plan.json site_centre_cm; main_street is the street row best aligned with the peak bearing at ~2.5x plaza radius; treeline at 1.25x the town extent radius; vista at 2.6x extent on the opposite side, looking back over the town to the peak. Peak found as the argmax of terrain/alpine_8k.png at world (100800, 208100), 3195 m from the plaza on bearing -12.8 deg.  AMENDED 2026-09-05: treeline and vista are NO LONGER bearing-derived. A bearing tells you where a thing is, not whether anything is in the way, and occlusion had never been traced on this route -- both stations framed something other than what they were named for. They are now derived by MEASURED framing (scripts/bench_station_derive.py): depth-band percentages, canopy inside the species' pixel band, and ridge columns, judged against a declared requirement. plaza and main_street are UNCHANGED and remain bearing-derived; main_street's own defect (a camera that cannot see out, carrying the lowest GPU budget of the four) is still OPEN and unexplained.
spline._LIMIT_STATED_PLAINLY: These are FIXED STATIONS sampled along the route, not a moving camera. They measure STEADY-STATE cost per zone. They do NOT measure streaming transients, World Partition pop-in, or shader-compile hitches on first traversal -- a moving-camera variant would, and is the natural extension. Reporting these as 'the flythrough cost' without that sentence would overstate what was measured.
spline._eye_height: ground is TRACED per station in-editor, never taken from the heightmap. This project shipped a render/collide divergence of p90 30.98 m once; the heightmap is not the collidable world.

spline._fov_horizontal_deg: RULED 2026-09-05. SET on the viewport and READ BACK at every station; perf_flythrough REFUSES a station whose read-back disagrees by more than 0.05 deg, and refuses to run at all if this key is absent. WHY IT HAD TO BE DECLARED: until now nothing in this path set or recorded an FOV, so every figure on the board -- including the RATIFIED budgets -- was captured at whatever the viewport happened to be. FOV is the parameter that most directly decides how much geometry is in frame, so a GPUTime p90 without one is not a reproducible measurement. 90 is UE's default editor horizontal FOV and is therefore the most likely value the 2026-08-29 baseline was taken at -- but that is an inference, not a record, and the pre-2026-09-05 baseline remains of unknown FOV.
spline._frame_resolution: For STATION RENDERS via scripts/shoot.py (HighResShot), which CAN be given an explicit resolution. This is the ratified target resolution from `target.resolution`. It is NOT the resolution of the perf capture -- see viewport_size_policy.
spline._viewport_size_policy: The STANDALONE class declares -ResX/-ResY and reads the resolution back from CsvProfiler metadata (perf_standalone: requested 3840x2160, res_matches_request true per zone), so the budget's resolution IS declared and verified. HISTORY, retired with the editor class 2026-09-10 (audit finding: this block still asserted the editor class inside the file that rejects it): under the EDITOR class the resolution could only be observed, never imposed -- the viewport was the editor window, and declaring a resolution the toolchain cannot impose is the `Tiling`-scalar defect (a parameter that exists and is never written). That lesson stands; the class it applied to does not source budgets any more.

budgets._status: RE-RATIFIED BY RYAN 2026-09-10, from E3's STANDALONE 4K measurement (_verify/perf/standalone_2026-09-07/perf_standalone.json; 2,670-3,737 frames per station at the CURRENT re-derived cameras). The 2026-08-30 editor-derived budgets are REJECTED -- see RECIPES R-PERFBUDGET REJECTED and _MEASUREMENT_CLASS above. These are law; check_perf enforces them and refuses editor-sourced artefacts.
budgets._method: GPU budget = standalone 4K p90 x 1.2, ROUNDED UP to 0.5 ms per zone (8.334->10.5, 5.945->7.5, 5.578->7.0, 6.988->8.5). Game thread: flat 6.0 ms all zones (standalone p90 runs 3.85-4.05; the per-zone editor figures measured the harness). Frame: 16.6 ms on FrameTime p90. Plus the 10% tolerance in `gates`.
budgets._HISTORY_2026_08_30: The prior ratification (GPU 12.0/8.0/10.0/12.5, Game 12.0/13.0/13.5/13.0, editor class, 1.35x/1.25x allowances) and its finding 'the game thread is the binding thread at all four zones' are RETIRED WITH THE CLASS: the editor game thread tracked the 60 Hz clamp (13.9-14.15 everywhere), so the binding-thread finding was an instrument artefact. In the standalone class the GPU binds at every zone. The old numbers stay quoted here because R13-class calibration history must remain findable.

per_zone_game_ms._metric: GameThreadTime p90, milliseconds, STANDALONE class -- flat by ruling; the game thread is NOT content-driven at these stations (spread 5.2%)

budgets._WHY_THOSE_THREE_ARE_STILL_NULL: NOT MEASURED, and a number invented for them would be exactly the untested bar this recipe's _order_is_deliberate note warns against. The CSV profiler run captures FrameTime, GameThreadTime, RenderThreadTime, GPUTime and RHIThreadTime and nothing else. Getting the other three needs additional CSV categories (`CsvCategory <name> enable` -- and note the ARGUMENT IS THE WORD 'enable', because `CsvCategory VSM 1` is a SILENT NO-OP that this project already paid for) or a `stat rhi` capture path that does not exist yet. Declared null and unmeasured rather than guessed.

asset_rules._what: The hard asset-side rule the forge must obey. scripts/asset_forge.py REFUSES or decimates to comply -- a budget nothing enforces is a wish.

max_tris._kit_module: the 15 measured kit modules run 10.1k-19.7k Nanite tris, so 20k is the measured ceiling of what is already accepted, not an invented one
max_tris._hero_prop: the church is a one-off focal anchor and may carry more than a wall module

max_texture_mb._kit_module: the kit's own per-module texture set runs ~47 MB of .uasset; 64 leaves headroom without licensing a doubling

gates._ratified: RE-RATIFIED BY RYAN 2026-09-10 from the E3 standalone 4K p90 (see budgets._status). The 2026-08-30 editor-class ratification is retired with its class; the standing plaza-Game RED (14.00 vs 12.00, editor artefact 20260905_fov90) is CLOSED AS AN INSTRUMENT ARTEFACT -- the number tracked the editor's 60 Hz clamp, not the content. check_perf refuses editor-sourced artefacts from this date.
gates._require_measurement_class: RULED 2026-09-10: an artefact must declare _measurement_class containing 'STANDALONE' or check_perf refuses it. An editor-class number tracking the tick clamp reported a RED for four days that no content change could have caused or cured.
gates._tolerance: a zone is RED when it exceeds its budget by more than this fraction. Run-to-run spread on this machine is real; a zero-tolerance gate would cry wolf and get ignored, which is worse than no gate.
gates._require_residency: measure_frame_cost REFUSES (exit 6) when residency is undeclared on a partitioned world. A cost number taken with regions unloaded is a measurement of an emptier world.
